stops.note: one who acts on his own authority; the root of English 'authentic'
spoken Greek of Constantinople softened the word to 'afendis', lord
a title for scholars, clerics and officials; Turkey's 1934 law abolishing titles ended its official use
in British-ruled Egypt it came to mean the Western-educated middle class of clerks and officials

current_meaning: a title of respect for an educated or official man in Ottoman-era lands
